text: Now Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, took action, along with Dathan and Abiram sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, descendants of Reuben.
They rose up against Moses, together with two hundred and fifty men of Israel, leaders of the community, appointed members of the assembly, men of reputation.

They gathered against Moses and Aaron and said to them, "You have gone too far! The whole community is holy, every one of them, and the LORD is among them. Why then do you set yourselves above the LORD's assembly?"
When Moses heard this, he fell facedown.

Then he said to Korah and all his followers: "In the morning the LORD will make known who belongs to him and who is holy, and he will bring that one near to himself. The one he chooses he will bring near to himself.
Do this: take censers for yourselves, Korah and all your followers.
Tomorrow put fire in them and lay incense on them before the LORD. The man the LORD chooses will be the holy one. You Levites have gone too far!"
Moses also said to Korah, "Listen now, you Levites!

Is it not enough for you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the rest of the community of Israel and brought you near to himself, to do the work at the LORD's dwelling and to stand before the community and serve them?
He has brought you near, you and all your fellow Levites with you, and now you seek the priesthood as well!
So it is against the LORD that you and all your followers have banded together. And Aaron—what is he, that you should grumble against him?"

versions.text: It is against the LORD that you and all your followers have banded together. What is Aaron, that you should grumble against him?"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew opens with לָכֵן ("therefore/so"), which links this verse to Moses' preceding argument; leaving it out weakens the logical flow. Adding a light connective preserves the link and improves the spoken rhythm.

text: Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, "We will not come.
Is it not enough that you brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness? Must you also lord it over us?
Besides, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you gouge out the eyes of these men? We will not come!"
Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, "Do not accept their offering. I have not taken so much as a donkey from them, nor have I wronged a single one of them."
Then Moses said to Korah, "You and all your followers are to appear before the LORD tomorrow—you and they and Aaron.
Each man is to take his censer and put incense on it—two hundred and fifty censers in all—and present it before the LORD. You and Aaron are each to bring your censer as well."
So each man took his censer, put fire in it, laid incense on it, and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
When Korah had gathered the whole community against them at the entrance to the tent of meeting, the glory of the LORD appeared to the entire community.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Separate yourselves from this community, and I will consume them in an instant."
But they fell facedown and cried out, "O God, God of the spirits of all flesh, will you be angry with the whole community when only one man sins?"
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Say to the community: Get away from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram."

versions.text: "Say to the community: Move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has the singular מִשְׁכַּן ("dwelling") and the phrase מִסָּבִיב ("from around"), which is echoed again in verse 27. The present rendering loses "from around" and shifts to a plural noun; matching the wording of verse 27 also keeps the narrative consistent.

text: Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
He said to the community, "Move back from the tents of these wicked men! Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away because of all their sins."

versions.text: He warned the community, "Move back from the tents of these wicked men! Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away because of all their sins."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb is the ordinary "spoke/said"; "warned" adds an interpretive element not present in the text, though the warning tone is already carried by the quoted words.

text: So they moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram had come out and were standing at the entrances of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little ones.
Then Moses said, "This is how you will know that the LORD has sent me to do all these things and that it was not my own idea:
If these men die a natural death and suffer only what usually comes to people, then the LORD has not sent me.

But if the LORD brings about something entirely new—if the ground opens its mouth and swallows them with everything they own, so that they go down alive to the realm of the dead—then you will know that these men have treated the LORD with contempt."
As soon as he finished speaking these words, the ground under them split open.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, along with all Korah's men and all their possessions.
They went down alive to the realm of the dead, with everything they owned. The earth closed over them, and they perished from among the assembly.
At their cries, all the Israelites around them fled, shouting, "The earth is going to swallow us too!"
And fire came out from the LORD and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who were offering the incense.
